newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares stable on quiet support - traders.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares stable on quiet support - traders.

text.p: Quiet buying supported some leading Russian shares on Tuesday, traders said, adding the market was stable.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 leading shares closed at 355.35, slightly off Monday's closing 355.46, on a slim $27.1 million total market volume.

"It's quite an interesting situation on the market -- while there's a certain absence of buying interest from major operators, the market looks stable," said United Financial Group trader Maxim Perlin.
"We're seeing targetted buys, but it's not general market growth -- it's more of a long-term perspective."
National utility UES EESR.RTS firmed to $0.3140 from $0.3135, while international long-distance provider Rostelekom edged up to $3.81 from $3.76.
Rostelekom announced 1996 pre-tax profit of 1.11 trillion roubles but said first quarter 1997 pre-tax profits fell to 467.5 billion roubles from 767.5 billion in 1996.
Prospekt chief trader Andrei Ippolitov saw an overall increase in market stability, and said prices could rise by the end of June if existing support was not broken.
"Many portfolio investors have cashed out and are not buying. Let them get used to the new levels -- they'll see that the market isn't falling."
Perlin said investors were quietly buying large blocks of oil companies LUKoil and Surgutneftegaz and retail bank Sberbank.
LUKoil LKOH.RTS edged up to $15.09 from $14.98, Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS firmed to $0.864 from $0.854, and Sberbank SBER.RTS rose to $158.70 from $143.90.
